prompt:
Write 9 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim, in time order. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1408; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant later added small details, but the account stayed the same.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- A few old scratches may be older than this crash.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened after the insured reported a collision at an intersection while the claimant's vehicle was turning left across oncoming traffic. The claimant was not represented by counsel at intake and gave a first statement by phone.
Entry 2: Confirmed the driver is named on the policy and that coverage was in force on the day of loss. No issues with the policy period were found.
Entry 3: Reviewed the police report, which places the claimant inside the vehicle at the scene. Responding officers and the one other driver's statement are consistent with the claimant's version of events.
Entry 4: Photos submitted by the claimant show the rear quarter panel and bumper damage in a pattern that matches the described impact. A few older scratches are visible on the lower panel, which may predate this loss and will be noted separately in the estimate.
Entry 5: No independent witnesses were located after canvassing the area. Scene photos confirm several details of the layout and vehicle positions but do not capture the moment of impact.
Entry 6: Claimant reported neck and back strain and began a treatment plan with a primary care provider. The type of injury and the force involved in the collision appear to fit well together.
Entry 7: Medical records show treatment followed a usual course and tapered as the claimant improved. No prior injury to the same body area is known from the records requested so far.
Entry 8: In a follow-up call the claimant added a few small details about the sequence of events, such as the signal timing and the position of the other car. The core account has remained the same across all statements.
Entry 9: Nothing in the file suggests the damage occurred before the policy coverage began. Estimate is being finalized based on the matched damage, and the file will be reviewed again when the final treatment bills arrive.
